headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist by default when Haystack feeds Kotaemon’s document-processing and API-backed workflows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Haystack can call MCP servers and REST APIs, while Kotaemon ingests documents, HTML, PDFs, and chat transcripts. If Haystack outputs are routed into Kotaemon’s web UI or file workspace, attacker-controlled content can be treated as instructions. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so the interaction is plausible in default RAG-style use.
conditions: IF Haystack outputs are copied into Kotaemon prompts or uploaded documents
IF Kotaemon parses Haystack-produced text as trusted instructions without provenance tags
mitigations: Add a fixed delimiter and provenance header before passing content between agents
Disable automatic ingestion of agent-generated text into Kotaemon prompts
Review one sample handoff for instruction-like strings before enabling the pair
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware parsing or content signing

B_data_leakage.rationale: Haystack has broad network egress and MCP/REST access, while Kotaemon handles documents, chat transcripts, and API keys in ./ktem_app_data. If both share a workspace or the same operator account, sensitive files can flow from Kotaemon into Haystack’s outbound requests or retrieval context. That creates a realistic exfiltration path with broad blast radius.
conditions: IF both agents can read the same workspace or mounted volume
IF Kotaemon indexes files containing API keys or confidential documents
IF Haystack forwards retrieved content to external APIs or MCP endpoints
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories and mounts
Remove secrets from Kotaemon’s indexed corpus before running Haystack
Restrict Haystack egress to approved endpoints only
Run a quick test with a harmless file to confirm no cross-read occurs
requires-engineering: add per-document allowlists and redaction

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Haystack can write through MCP/REST-connected tools, and Kotaemon supports multiple instances plus a local app-data directory. If both are pointed at the same mutable workspace or shared backend, concurrent writes can overwrite indexes, caches, or generated artifacts. The profiles do not show locking, so conflict is plausible and not prevented by default.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or database
IF one agent rebuilds indexes while the other updates the same artifacts
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory
Pause one agent during index rebuilds or bulk writes
Check for file collisions in ./ktem_app_data before enabling concurrency
requires-engineering: add locking or transactional writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Haystack is a search-RAG system that can generate retrieved facts, and Kotaemon is a customer-support RAG app that can present or act on those outputs. If Kotaemon treats Haystack’s answers as authoritative, retrieval errors or hallucinations can cascade into user-facing support responses or downstream actions. No verification step is documented in either profile.
conditions: IF Kotaemon uses Haystack output as the final answer source
IF no human or rule-based verification step is inserted between them
mitigations: Require a human review step for high-impact answers
Compare Haystack output against a second source before responding
Add a confidence threshold that blocks low-confidence answers
Log source passages alongside final responses
requires-engineering: implement citation and verification gating

E_compliance.rationale: Haystack touches anonymous usage statistics, while Kotaemon handles documents, chat transcripts, and API keys and may send them to third-party model APIs. If EU or regulated content is routed through Kotaemon into Haystack-backed or external inference paths, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so the mismatch is plausible.
conditions: IF regulated documents or personal data are indexed in Kotaemon
IF those records are forwarded to external model APIs or Haystack-backed services
IF retention or deletion policies differ between the two systems
mitigations: Classify the data before indexing it in Kotaemon
Exclude regulated documents from external API calls
Document retention settings for both systems side by side
Verify deletion on one sample record in each system
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
